⚡ What OctoSlave Can Do

OctoSlave is a single autonomous agent that plans, executes, verifies, and iterates. Point it at a task — code, research, analysis, or a full multi-agent investigation — and it works end-to-end until the job is done.

1

💻 Code & engineering

Explores repos, writes/refactors/debugs code, runs tests, builds and deploys. Supports Python (uv), JS, Go, Rust, C/C++, and more.

agentic loop
2

🌐 Web research

DuckDuckGo search, full-page & PDF extraction, and an intelligent BFS site crawler. Synthesises findings across sources.

live web
3

🧬 Bio & chemistry

Direct REST access to UniProt, PubChem, ChEMBL, RCSB PDB, AlphaFold, GEO, ENA + RDKit for molecule analysis.

domain tools
4

🧪 Self-verifying

Writes a numbered plan before acting, grades its own completion (DONE / PARTIAL / FAILED), and nudges out of repeated failures.

self-check
5

🔁 Autonomous Lab

Self-organizing research team — a Director builds up to 10 specialists, a Critic gates the plan, produces an HTML report.

multi-agent
6

🔌 MCP & remote

Plugs in 21+ external tools (Git, GitHub, browser, DBs) via MCP. Runs tools on remote SSH hosts with GPU access.

extensible

🚀 How to Use It

Get started in 3 steps

1

Install

Download the bundled installer — no Python required. macOS, Windows, and Linux (AppImage) all available.

2

Configure

Add an e-INFRA CZ or NVIDIA NIM key — or go fully local with Ollama for complete privacy.

3

Run

Type a task and watch OctoSlave plan, execute, and report back — interactively or one-shot.

Web UI (browser)

Start the visual interface in one command — plan, execute, and review results in your browser. Works locally (127.0.0.1:7860) or share the link to let others join.

$ ots web

Backends — pick your trade-off

Any custom OpenAI-compatible provider can be connected — just set the endpoint and API key in ots config. Built-in backends include e-INFRA CZ, NVIDIA NIM, and Ollama.

🏛️ Working Modes

A single capable agent — fast and direct

One model drives the entire task. Perfect for everyday coding, quick questions, and tasks where a single strong model is enough. Low token cost and lowest latency.

$ ots run "build a todo API"

🐙 Improved — a unified model council

Instead of one model, a lightweight coordinator routes each step between three role-specialized models behind one agent surface — so a diverse pool beats any single model. You still talk to one agent.

The three roles

RoleDefault modelResponsibility
🔧 Workerkimi-k.3Drives the tool loop — reads, writes, edits, runs commands.
🧠 Thinkerkimi-k.3Orients the workspace, writes the execution plan, course-corrects on repeated errors.
🔍 Verifierglm-5.2Independent critic — reviews risky actions before they run and grades completion.

How routing works

  • Easy steps (read-only) run on the Worker alone — fast, no extra calls.
  • Risky steps (file edits, bash, background jobs) are reviewed by the Verifier before execution.
  • Hard steps (stalls, repeated errors) pull in the Thinker for course correction.
  • Diversity escalation — when the Worker gets stuck, it switches to a different model family automatically.
  • Completion gate — the Verifier grades the final result and can send it back for another round.
$ ots improved run "analyse this dataset"

⚡ Ultra — multi-model debate for the hardest tasks

A deeper tier on top of Improved mode. A diverse panel (one model per family) drafts ideas in isolation, then an aggregator synthesizes the strongest plan. At completion the panel independently grades the work and resolves their verdicts.

Ultra at a glance

Planning debate

Each panelist drafts a plan in isolation → aggregator synthesizes one stronger plan.

Completion debate

Panel grades the finished work → aggregator resolves verdicts. A real defect any one spots is surfaced; nitpicks don't deadlock.

AspectUltraImprovedStandard
Panel3-model debate3-role council1 model
PlanningIsolated drafts + synthesisSingle ThinkerSingle model
CompletionPanel grades + resolvesSingle VerifierSelf-assessed
Cost / latencyHighestMediumLowest
 
$ ots improved --ultra run "prove this conjecture"
/ultra on | off | status

🧪 Science & Lab Options

For researchers who need real, reproducible results — not just summaries. Conversational orchestration and autonomous multi-agent teams, with live HPC offloading and FAIR data curation.

🧬

Science tab /science

Chat-first research orchestrator. You stay in the loop — every plot, table, and dataset appears inline for comment-driven refinement.

  • 🧠 Spins up specialists on demand (Structural Biologist, Data Wrangler, …)
  • 📊 Presents plots & tables inline — edit or regenerate specific outputs
  • 🧬 Full bio/chem toolbox: UniProt, PubChem, ChEMBL, PDB, AlphaFold, GEO, ENA, RDKit
  • 🖥️ Offloads long jobs to Slurm/PBS or detached background processes
  • 🔬 Curates messy data into FAIR datasets (datapackage.json)
  • 📚 Finds the most relevant current literature (Europe PMC)
web-only
🧪

Autonomous Research tab /lab

Self-organizing research team as a batch pipeline. Hand off a whole problem and let a team run it end-to-end.

  • 🎯 Director builds a custom team of up to 10 specialists per task
  • 🛡️ Critic challenges every plan before implementation
  • 🧙 Runtime tool foundry — agents build new tools mid-run
  • 👥 Add teammates or connect MCP servers on demand
  • 📝 Produces a self-contained HTML report
  • ✋ Human-in-the-loop: step-mode approval gates or full autonomy
batch pipeline

Extend & connect

🔌 MCP tools

Plug in ~21 curated servers: Git, GitHub, Playwright browser, SQLite/Postgres, Slack, Notion, Google Drive, and more.

$ /mcp registry          # browse catalog
$ /mcp install github       # one-click install
$ /mcp add mysrv "uvx …"    # custom server

💻 Remote execution

Run tools on a remote SSH host — for remote GPUs, compute clusters, or data that lives on a server. Add once, switch instantly. Below is the Web UI's connection panel — click the highlighted button to switch the active backend to your remote PC.

$ ots run "train model" --remote gpu01
/remote add | list | <id> | local
